body.x: Torrential rain runs off paved streets that cannot absorb it, and retaining walls and slopes weakened by water give way. At the same time, plastic waste that is dirty or made of mixed materials is hard to recycle and ends up incinerated or in landfill. Cities facing the climate crisis tend to deal with these as separate problems.

WES-TEC Global Co., Ltd. treats them as one. The company, founded in 2017 and based in Giheung-gu, Yongin, describes itself as a climate-tech company whose mission is to deliver "standardized technology for responding to climate disasters." Led by CEO Ayeon Choi, it was selected as a winner in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards. In its application, the company said it would not be taking part in the exhibition itself.

WES-TEC Global says its engineering team, led by CTO Kyoungyoung Choi, who has 35 years of experience in the industry, works from the principle that an eco-friendly alternative cannot scale unless it is economically viable. On that basis, the company says, it has developed construction materials that address disaster-resilient infrastructure and resource circulation together.

Its first core product is the Joint-Gap Permeable Block. The company says conventional permeable blocks depend on tiny pores inside the block and lose performance as the pores clog, whereas its block channels water through gaps formed by hinge joints between blocks and through a storage space underneath. WES-TEC Global reports an infiltration rate of 8 mm/s, about 80 times the standard of Korea's Public Procurement Service (PPS), and says field sites have confirmed that permeability holds up 12 years after installation. A cement-free version, co-developed with Samsung C&T, was designated an Innovative Product by the PPS in 2026, which the company says opens the way into the public procurement market. The block has been installed at sites including Chiaksan National Park, sidewalks, public plazas and parking lots.

The second product is the 3D Interlocking Retaining Wall Block, which locks together front to back, side to side and top to bottom like LEGO bricks to form a single structure. According to the company, it can be installed without a concrete foundation and used for restoring ecological streams, protecting riverbanks, preventing landslides and controlling coastal erosion. WES-TEC Global says it has been installed at more than 3,000 sites in Korea and overseas, including an emergency helipad on Jebudo Island and a coastal protection and parking lot expansion project on Janggjado Island in Gunsan. Those projects, it says, showed the block can be installed quickly in coastal areas while seawater flows in and out, without cofferdam work.

The third is Eco-C CUBE, a retaining wall block made from waste plastic, together with REVOCLE, the system that produces it. The company says Eco-C CUBE recreates in waste plastic the 3D interlocking design already used in concrete blocks. The system accepts contaminated, mixed-material plastic waste that has long been excluded from recycling, such as discarded fishing nets, buoys and agricultural film, and forms it by low-temperature extrusion without washing or sorting. WES-TEC Global says its proprietary NewCycling process keeps polymer chains intact, giving the block a compressive strength of more than 25 MPa, higher than that of concrete retaining wall products, and that processing costs and installation time are lower. The company says it also produces no wastewater or sorting residue.

The company cites outside recognition for the product. The SDX Carbon Reduction Certification Center has certified that every ton of waste plastic processed reduces CO₂ emissions by 2.99 tons. Eco-C CUBE won a Silver Award at the 2025 Edison Awards and was named a CES Innovation Awards 2026 Honoree, and the company was selected as a Sprout Company by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT). It received Venture Company certification (Innovation Growth type) in 2025 along with official recognition of its corporate R&D center, and it is pursuing R&D and commercialization with Korea Land & Housing Corporation (LH), MOLIT and Nature & Environment.

On the technical side, WES-TEC Global says it has completed a pilot production line for REVOCLE and is applying AI to the production system to analyze the material composition and contamination level of incoming feedstock in real time. It expects this to lower melting temperatures by an average of 10% to 30%, cutting production costs, and to allow real-time calculation of carbon reductions. The company holds more than 10 domestic patents and numerous design registrations, and says it has filed patents in the U.S., the EU, Japan, India, Vietnam and Indonesia.

Overseas, the company says it exports technology more than finished products. It reports numerous installations of retaining wall and permeable blocks in Brazil, retaining wall block installations in Japan, and projects based on technical cooperation in Laos. In Germany, it is scheduled to install permeable blocks at the headquarters of the energy company Mainova in October 2026, which it expects to serve as a foothold in Europe. In September 2026, it introduced its technologies to the European construction market at an LH-hosted event during a Paris architecture exhibition. In Africa, the company says the ambassadors of Angola, Kenya and Tanzania visited in person to express interest in technical cooperation, and that it proposed a pilot covering 1.5 km of the Ghanaian coast during a meeting with the president of Ghana.

WES-TEC Global says it targets any country facing plastic pollution, climate disasters or pressure to cut carbon emissions. In its view, developing countries that lack washing and sorting infrastructure can turn plastic waste into disaster-resilient building materials locally, while developed countries can secure verified carbon reductions and climate adaptation infrastructure. It names infrastructure buyers and plastic waste generators as its key customers: municipal river and disaster safety officials, civil and landscape design and purchasing staff at large construction companies, coastal local governments, fisheries cooperatives and packaging producers with extended producer responsibility (EPR) obligations, and, abroad, coastal and infrastructure ministries in developing countries and Pacific island nations threatened by rising seas.

The company's main difficulty is proof at scale. Overseas buyers and governments want to see the technology proven commercially, and WES-TEC Global says a production facility in Korea processing 10 tons or more of plastic waste a day would speed its adoption worldwide. Building such a plant requires significant capital, and the company says it is raising investment for it.

It describes its plan as filling gaps in the recycling system rather than replacing it. Plastics that conventional methods can recycle should stay in circulation, the company says, while contaminated or mixed plastic that cannot be recycled can become Eco-C CUBE, which it says reduces demand for cement and steel rebar and, buried as part of civil structures, amounts to effectively permanent carbon storage. The company would first build the Korean plant, then begin full-scale REVOCLE exports in 2027. It also plans a platform linking plastic waste generators, Eco-C CUBE manufacturers, and businesses and public institutions that take part in climate mitigation projects, so they can share the resulting carbon reduction credits. Its revenue model rests on four streams: equipment sales, waste treatment fees, product sales and carbon credits.

Regional plans follow local needs. In Africa, WES-TEC Global would begin with the Ghana pilot and expand to Angola, Kenya, Tanzania and beyond, and in Europe it would use the Mainova installation as a foothold. The company is also proposing the "Poseidon Project" to the Korean government and the international community, under which plastic collected from garbage patches in the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans would be made into Eco-C CUBE on site and supplied for coastal protection in island nations threatened by rising seas. In the company's words, it aims to establish its technology and carbon reduction framework as a global standard.

Now in its third year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Technology Expo) is a future-industry exhibition that brings together and links innovative technologies in future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. It will be held from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at EXCO in Daegu. Centered on the theme "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," it shares industry trends and core technologies through AI-based technology exhibitions, conferences and lectures by experts from Korea and abroad, and networking programs.
